scenario.title: Verification Test Setup and Reporting
scenario.initial_description: An engineer prepares a verification test, runs the evaluation, checks the results, and writes a short report. If something looks wrong, the engineer investigates and shares the result with related people.

reference_workflow.goal: Run a verification test and distribute a summarized result report.

activities.name: Review report and request clarification if needed

decisions.condition: Are the result files complete and readable?
Do the results contain abnormal patterns?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Result file collection is repetitive and follows a standard folder or repository pattern.
Completeness and basic validity checks can be rule-based.
Report drafting can be supported by template filling and result summarization.

missing_information.gap: No distinction between who prepares the test versus who runs it — could be the same engineer or different roles
missing_information.why_it_matters: Role separation affects whether handoffs exist, which in turn affects automation boundaries and access control requirements

missing_information.gap: No systems or tools mentioned for test execution, result capture, or report writing
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing the systems involved, it is impossible to assess integration feasibility or identify automation entry points

missing_information.gap: No specification of what inputs are needed to prepare the verification test (e.g., test specifications, requirements documents, configurations)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Undefined inputs block upstream automation and make it unclear when the process can legitimately start

missing_information.gap: The report format, destination, and required content are not described
missing_information.why_it_matters: Ambiguous output definition prevents assessment of whether report generation can be automated or templated

missing_information.gap: The criteria for deciding 'something looks wrong' are not defined — no threshold, rule, or metric is specified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without explicit decision logic, this branch cannot be automated or even consistently executed manually

missing_information.gap: No description of what happens if the investigation does not resolve the issue — no escalation path or retry logic mentioned
missing_information.why_it_matters: Missing exception handling creates dead ends in the workflow that could stall the process or cause data loss

missing_information.gap: No information on how often this workflow runs (per day, per sprint, per release, etc.)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Frequency is a primary driver of automation ROI calculation and resource allocation decisions

missing_information.gap: No time estimates are given for any individual step (preparation, execution, result checking, report writing, investigation)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without effort data, it is impossible to quantify automation savings or prioritize which steps to automate first

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether test results are stored in a structured, machine-readable format or are manually recorded
missing_information.why_it_matters: Unstructured or manually recorded results would require OCR or NLP processing before automation is viable

missing_information.gap: No upstream dependencies are mentioned — it is unknown what must be ready or approved before the engineer can start preparing the test
missing_information.why_it_matters: Hidden dependencies can block automation triggers and cause incomplete process modeling

missing_information.gap: No mention of whether sharing results with related people uses email, a ticketing system, a collaboration tool, or another channel
missing_information.why_it_matters: The notification and sharing mechanism determines whether that step can be automated and what APIs or connectors are needed

missing_information.gap: No approval or sign-off step is described before the report is finalized or shared
missing_information.why_it_matters: If approvals are required but undocumented, automating report distribution without them could violate governance policies
